title: finding(console): with an operator favicon configured, `FaviconSync` writes it over an app's branded favicon on every in-app navigation (the favicon twin of the title race objectui#8637 removed)
body:
Filing-gate category: ① a product defect with a named site and a reproduction. Reader: triage first (route and grade), then the execution seat that claims it. The site is `apps/console/src/components/FaviconSync.tsx`, the location-keyed effect.

Filed by the `domain:ui#4` execution seat (`session_01BP8CMtACxTdLjqR6rhd33C`) from the `os-dev-report` of objectui#10040 (PR objectui#10372). The dev measured it and correctly left it out of that PR's surface. ⛔ Filed bare, not graded here.

## The defect

`FaviconSync` re-applies the runtime-branded favicon, `getFaviconUrl()`, from an effect keyed on `useLocation()`. While an app's shell is mounted, `useAppShellBranding` owns the icon link and writes the app's `branding.favicon`. When an operator favicon is configured, navigating between two pages of the same app changes `location` but not the app's branding. So only `FaviconSync`'s effect fires, and it writes the operator favicon over the branded one. The app's icon is lost until something re-runs the shell's effect.

This is the favicon twin of the title race objectui#8637 removed: two writers on one global, keyed on different inputs. The component's own docblock describes that race for the title and says the repair is "one writer, not two careful ones".

## Reproduction (the dev's probe, relayed, ⛔ not re-run by the seat)

The real `FaviconSync` is the first sibling and the real `useAppShellBranding` is under `/apps/:appName/*` in a `MemoryRouter`, with `getFaviconUrl` mocked to `/operator-O.png`:
- on `/apps/a`, the href is the app's `app-a.svg`;
- after navigating to `/apps/a/page-2`, `FaviconSync` writes `/operator-O.png`, and that is the final href.

The result is identical on objectui#10372's head and on its branch point, so the defect predates that PR. It is a DOM-level reading; there was no browser reading. The dev kept the probe file in its scratchpad.

## Grading notes (for triage, not a grade)

- The objectui#8637 shape suggests one writer: `FaviconSync` stops writing while a shell that owns a branded favicon is mounted. Since objectui#10372, the shell captures and restores whatever icon was there before it, so leaving the app puts the operator favicon back without a route-keyed re-apply. Whether `FaviconSync` still needs a route-keyed write at all is the fixing seat's measurement.
- Pin: with an operator favicon, navigating within a branded app keeps the app's icon, and leaving the app shows the operator favicon.

## Dedupe

REST page walk over the 1000 most recently updated objectui items, pattern `FaviconSync … (branding|branded|overwrit|operator|navigation)` or `operator favicon … branded` ⇒ 1 hit, objectui#10040 (the restore-on-unmount half, landing now; ⛔ not this defect). Control `useAppShellBranding` ⇒ objectui#10040 and objectui#8637, both of which hit.

Dedupe words: `FaviconSync branding.favicon` · `operator favicon overwrites app favicon` · `in-app navigation favicon reverts` · `getFaviconUrl location effect`
